source.version_note: Published 9 July 2026, Journal of Healthcare Leadership 18:590498. The supplied file ends with references and a publisher page; the claimed extraction/evidence/quality appendices are absent.

citation.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare: Automation Bias, Deskilling, and Cognitive Implications – A Systematic Review

reading.source_scope_note: Narrative systematic-review synthesis with unresolved selection arithmetic, quality-threshold conflicts, search-cutoff violations and citation-to-claim mismatches. Useful as a lead list, not treated as independently validated primary evidence for new mechanisms or pooled GenAI effects.
access_limits: All 13 extracted pages read, including PRISMA diagram text, counts, synthesis, limitations and 50 references. Page 5 diagram also visually inspected to confirm the printed arithmetic mismatch. No claim to have read the 29 included studies.
Appendices A/B/C, Tables B1/C1, included-study extraction, full quality ratings and raw search results are absent from the supplied PDF and were not obtained externally.

Crossref metadata checked for Natali, Budzyn, Khan, Ueda, Ranji and McDermid references; PubMed metadata/search record checked for Budzyn's online date and the Choudhury/Chaudhry loop-paper identity. These are not full-text primary reviews.

study.databases: Abstract names four; methods names PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore and Google Scholar
study.quality_claim: 14 high at >=8/10 and 15 moderate at 6–7/10, but also says only above 70% retained

summary: No new behaviour promoted from this review. Preserve its leads for long-term skill retention and recursive training under existing entries, but flag them as noncorroborating boundary notes. Resolve the review's source and methods problems before relying on quantitative gains, newly named risks or the claimed 29-study GenAI synthesis.

findings.term: Deskilling concerns, observed performance changes and sustained skill loss require different evidence
findings.definition: Short-term assisted performance, clinicians' concerns and persistent loss of unaided competence are distinct outcomes; a narrative review must identify which each source actually measured.
findings.novelty_rationale: Strengthens the existing skill-loss boundary and preserves primary-study leads without treating the review's internally inconsistent synthesis as an additional independent longitudinal demonstration.

evidence.quote: regarding long-term deskilling and cognitive erosion remain largely theoretical and warrant further longitudinal
whether cognitive degradation is transient or persistent

findings.evidence_scope: The review explicitly acknowledges limited longitudinal evidence but elsewhere says numerous studies demonstrated deskilling. It cites a colonoscopy observational primary and a mixed-method review; their full texts remain unread, and their dates conflict with its stated search cutoff.
findings.boundary: Do not infer reduced skill acquisition, actual erosion of previously acquired skill and altered assisted performance from the same metric. Colonoscopy detection rate is not automatically general diagnostic accuracy or a generative-language-model effect. Original design, comparator, temporal changes and unaided follow-up need verification.

findings.term: Self-referential learning loop is a recursive-data lead, not a new proven collapse mechanism
findings.definition: Reusing AI-influenced outputs as future training material can create a feedback pathway that needs separate validation for data diversity, error amplification and actual model degradation.
findings.novelty_rationale: The named loop overlaps recursive synthetic-data training already covered by model collapse; the review does not establish an additional independent mechanism, training event or collapse result.

evidence.quote: wherein persistent human reliance on AI not only diminishes clinicians’ skills but also taints

findings.evidence_scope: Secondary theoretical account citing Choudhury and Chaudhry (2024), DOI 10.2196/56764. Primary title/abstract metadata support that the proposed loop concerns AI-generated data feeding learning algorithms, but the complete paper is unread. No recursive model training is conducted by this review.
findings.boundary: The feedback pathway, human deskilling and model collapse are different claims. A fixed deployed model does not retrain automatically from a conversation. Synthetic data can be filtered or usefully mixed with real data; demonstrate the actual data lineage and performance changes before claiming collapse.

findings.term: Traditional diagnostic AI and GenAI evidence must not be pooled by label alone
findings.definition: Automation-bias results from conventional diagnostic classifiers do not become direct evidence about generative systems merely because a review presents them in a GenAI synthesis.
findings.novelty_rationale: Adds an evidence-type boundary, not a new automation-bias finding or additional independent study count.

evidence.quote: Studies focusing exclusively on non-generative predictive or classification AI systems were excluded unless
a generative component was explicitly evaluated
Automation bias in mammography: the impact of artificial intelligence BI-RADS suggestions on reader

findings.evidence_scope: The review's inclusion rule is GenAI-specific, while multiple cited diagnostic/radiology/colonoscopy examples do not establish an evaluated generative component in the supplied synthesis. The missing study table prevents a complete classification audit.
findings.boundary: Traditional automation evidence can inform hypotheses about GenAI but should retain its actual system, task and outcome. No assertion is made that every listed diagnostic system lacks generation; verify each original rather than transfer the review's heading to it.

methodological_limits: The abstract names four databases, while methods names six. Exact database-specific search dates, complete reproducible search syntax/export and a protocol registration are not supplied. Broad statements that PRISMA guarantees rigor are not a methodological validation.

PRISMA Figure 1 arithmetic: 11269−1179=10090 screened; 10090−9006=1084, not 84 sought. This leaves 1000 records unexplained. The final full-text subtraction 84−55=29 and six exclusion reasons summing to 55 do reconcile.

Narrative screening gives a different pipeline and says 11269 after deduplication. Removing 4179 would leave 7090, not its stated 5653. Intermediate 3837/3734/2217/1686 counts are not reconciled with the diagram.

The title/abstract process is called independent but says each reviewer screened 50% with 20% overlap, not full duplicate screening. The denominator and procedure behind kappa .87 and 42 disagreements need clarification; the second reviewer is unnamed in the supplied acknowledgments/declarations.

The quality section says 14 high and 15 moderate studies at 6–7/10 were included, but only studies above 70% were retained. Scores of 6 or 7 cannot meet that strict threshold. The absent CASP checklist variants and per-study ratings prevent reconciliation.

Journal quartiles, citation metrics and impact factors are not study-level risk-of-bias criteria. Restricting Q1–Q4 outlets does not substitute for appropriate design-specific appraisal and may introduce selection effects.

The stated window ends June 2025 and last search is 15 July 2025. Crossref dates show Natali online 27 August and Khan 4 August; PubMed gives Budzyn online 12 August. Later inclusion may reflect an update, but no such update is documented. Their peer-reviewed versions cannot be assumed available within the stated search.

The claimed appendices and Tables B1/C1 are absent from this 13-page file, which ends in a publisher advertisement. Thus the exact 29 included identities, extracted outcomes, theme counts and quality scores cannot be audited from the supplied evidence.

Multiple reviews/umbrella reviews and conceptual papers overlap underlying studies. Counting 29 publications or 10 automation-bias mentions does not establish 29 independent datasets, prevalence, pooled effect size or evidential strength.

The methods exclude non-generative systems without an evaluated generative component, yet the synthesis includes general radiology/classifier/colonoscopy and HITL literature without documenting such a component. Findings must retain actual model type and cannot all support a GenAI-specific causal conclusion.

Ueda reference 30 is titled Fairness of artificial intelligence in healthcare: review and recommendations, but the synthesis attributes a GPT-4 versus GPT-3.5/Llama-2 radiology benchmark to it. The identified citation does not establish that claimed experiment; original evidence or the intended benchmark reference is needed.

Ranji reference 43 is titled Large Language Models—Misdiagnosing Diagnostic Excellence?, but the synthesis attributes a 30% decrease in endocrine diagnostic latency to it. Metadata alone do not support that quantitative clinical result; verify the intended primary before reuse.

Reference 50 is McDermid and colleagues' 2021 explainability article, while the discussion invokes recent provable ethical-firewall architectures. The citation-to-specific-claim match requires checking; it cannot be treated as demonstrated clinical guardrail efficacy.

The 40–45% efficiency, 88% dose-error reduction, 20% colonoscopy accuracy reduction and 30% endocrine latency claims use different or unspecified endpoints, comparators and denominators. They are not one comparable benefit/harm scale. Relative detection-rate change differs from percentage-point change and overall diagnostic accuracy.

Short-term accuracy, simulated decisions, anticipated skill loss and persistent acquired-skill erosion are repeatedly discussed together. The conclusion appropriately concedes predominantly short-term, heterogeneous evidence; stronger causal statements elsewhere need that qualification.

Ecological debounding is defined in the review but its attribution to the named primaries is unverified. Exact-phrase search did not independently resolve it. Absence of a search hit is not proof of fabrication; keep the lead pending rather than promote it as an established term.

Upskilling inhibition, AI chasm, cognitive partnership and distributed cognition are secondary labels or frameworks here, without adequate independent definitions/tests for new behavioural entries. The self-referential loop is theoretical, not an observed retraining process.

Explainability, human-in-the-loop and reskilling are proposed safeguards across disparate sources; this review does not estimate their causal effects or prove they prevent deskilling. Human presence alone is not demonstrated effective control.
Language exclusion is reported as 103 earlier and another 2 at full text; these stages should be distinguished, not treated as one total. The field's diversity is limited by English-only selection.
Crossref and PubMed checks establish bibliographic identities/dates only. No included primary full text, raw clinical dataset or code was independently reanalyzed in this file review.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Both syntheses combine empirical and conceptual sources. Counts of concerns or reasons are not prevalence or causal effects; the current review has additional unresolved screening/quality and inclusion-boundary problems.

Keep previously acquired skill erosion separate from inhibited acquisition and explicitly unmeasured responsibility mechanisms. A new review's repeated label does not resolve the need for longitudinal primary evidence.

Attractive headline claims must remain bounded by actual operational definitions and internal consistency. Proxy outcomes, unmeasured mechanisms and exploratory interpretations cannot silently become established causal results.

deferred.reason: The review calls it disconnection of clinical reasoning from real-world variability, but its primary attribution and established spelling/definition need verification. Do not confuse it with ecological fallacy or invent an independent validated mechanism.
Named secondarily without an adequate operational definition or direct evidence; do not automatically equate inhibited acquisition with erosion of acquired skill.
Mentioned as a concern and training target, but not defined or measured here. Read an appropriate primary psychological account before adding a distinct entry.
Related to existing recursive-data/model-collapse coverage. Primary metadata confirm the lead, but neither that metadata nor this review establishes a second independent collapse mechanism.

deferred.term: AI chasm / distributed cognition / cognitive partnership
deferred.reason: Broad theoretical labels with no new standalone behavioural definition/test in this review.
